title: A deadlock, caught with timed locks
expectedStdout:
t1 holds A, wants B: gave up after timeout
t2 holds B, wants A: gave up after timeout
both threads waited for each other: deadlock (circular wait)
tryThis: Make both threads lock `A` first, then `B`: both succeed. A single global lock order removes the circular wait.
Replace the timed locks by plain `std::mutex` + `lock()`: the program hangs until CppLab kills it after 10 s.
